fields.claim_quote: $$\binom{n}{2b+1}\left( \frac{2}{cn\cdot 2^f}\right)^{2b}= \frac{n^{2b+1}}{(2b+1)^{2b+1}} \frac{(2b+1)^{2b+1}}{2^f\cdot cn} = \frac{n}{1}\cdot\frac{1}{4^{f}\cdot n}=\frac{1}{4f}$$ Note that $n^{2b+1}=n^{2b}\cdot n = 2n = n$
fields.explanation: The full source explicitly permits discarding constant factors, so a lone finite numerical inequality is insufficient. The corrected evidence addresses the same quoted simplification n^(2b+1) to n with b=1 held fixed. For every constant C and threshold N there is n>=N with n^3>C*n. The Mathlib IsBigO refutation retains b=1,c=1,f=2 and treats n as the asymptotic variable; it does not claim that the legitimate factor 2 is significant.
fields.flaw: With b=1 fixed, the submitted side remark treats n^(2b+1)=n^3 as equivalent to n after discarding constant factors. This would require n^3=O(n), which is false. The legitimate simplification 2n=Theta(n) is not an error.
fields.problem: Rewriting an equation in the terms of Algorithmic complexity.
fields.source_context:
0001 | In [this](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~dga/papers/cuckoo-conext2014.pdf) paper (page 7 Eq. 3) the author derives the following: $$\binom{n}{2b+1}\left( \frac{2}{cn\cdot 2^f}\right)^{2b}=\Omega\left( \frac{n}{4^{bf}}\right)$$
0002 | I have tried to do the same below, but first some preliminaries. This is an analysis for algorithms and therefore constants can be erased. In this example, $b$ is a constant while $f$ is some $f$-bit fingerprint. I assume that $f$ is not treated as a constant here. $n$ is the number of elements and $c$ is just some constant. My take is the following, and note that the binomial coefficients is converted into its lower bound:
0003 | $$\binom{n}{2b+1}\left( \frac{2}{cn\cdot 2^f}\right)^{2b}= \frac{n^{2b+1}}{(2b+1)^{2b+1}} \frac{(2b+1)^{2b+1}}{2^f\cdot cn} = \frac{n}{1}\cdot\frac{1}{4^{f}\cdot n}=\frac{1}{4f}$$ Note that $n^{2b+1}=n^{2b}\cdot n = 2n = n$ because its algorithms and their analysis.. My result above is not the same as the one at the top of this question. How does the author derive that? How is $n$ kept in his result?
fields.witness: Keep b=1,c=1,f=2 and let n range over the natural numbers. The same quoted source simplification n^(2b+1) to n would require n^3=O(n). For every real constant C and natural threshold N, choose m>C and n=max(N,m)+2; then n>=N and n^3>C*n. Hence no eventual constant-factor bound exists, refuting the simplification under the source stated asymptotic convention.
